title: Proactive Thermal & Power Profiling Playbook
author: Evelyn Chen
content:
Summary

This playbook describes the proactive profiling, telemetry collection, and remediation patterns for GPU power, thermal, and power-capping interactions with the runtime kernel and scheduler. It is intended for SREs, runtime engineers, and performance owners who operate the runtime-kernel-manager, gpu-dispatcher, and telemetry-collector stacks.

Why this matters

- Thermal events, power capping, and sustained TDP-related throttling account for intermittent high tail latency and elevated token cost in our hosted and dedicated fleets.
- Early, structured profiling improves our ability to: prevent service degradation, inform kernel scheduling hints, and craft safe rollout/rollback gates for quantization or kernel changes that alter power draw.

Scope and assumptions

- Applies to: G4/G5-like GPU nodes in hosted/dedicated pools and to supported on-prem accelerator types where Tegra/CUSTOM-HW telemetry is forwarded to telemetry-collector.
- Not covered: facility-level rack cooling changes (contact infra).
- Dependencies: telemetry-collector >= 2.3.0, runtime-kernel-manager >= 1.8.1, gpu-dispatcher >= 3.0.

Key metrics and thresholds

| Metric | Warning threshold | Critical threshold | Note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| GPU junction temp (Tjunction, C) | 78 C | 88 C | sustained >1m triggers probe workflow |
| GPU power draw (W) | > 90% configured TDP for >30s | > 100% TDP (sustained or spiking) | power capping likely active |
| P99 runtime latency (ms) | > 250 ms | > 400 ms | across stationary workload sample |
| Kernel preemption count | > baseline + 50% | > baseline + 200% | indicates frequent kernel handoffs |
| Thermal throttling events | 1 per 10k requests | > 1 per 1k requests | immediate escalation |

Operational goals and SLO alignment

- Maintain fleet thermal-induced-degradation incidents to < 0.2% of customer requests per week.
- Ensure thermal-related rollbacks are executed within 30 minutes of detection for Dedicated customers.

Profiling procedures (lab and in-situ)

1) Synthetic lab profile (recommended before any kernel/quantization rollout)
   - Environment: perf-lab node with same SKU and driver stack as target fleet.
   - Steps:
     1. Deploy the exact model artifact and runtime-kernel-manager version to perf-lab.
     2. Run workload-sculptor to generate mixed-local-token workloads: `workload-sculptor --shape chat-heavy --concurrency 16 --duration 30m --seed <id>`.
     3. Collect GPU metrics: `telemetry-cli collect --node <node> --metrics gpu.temp,gpu.power,kernel.preempt --out ./lab-trace.json`
     4. Collect kernel traces: `sudo perf record -e sched_switch -a -- sleep 1800` then `perf script > perf-sched.txt`.
     5. Generate flamegraphs and power trace overlays: `flamegraph.pl perf-sched.txt > flame.svg` and `power-annotate --trace lab-trace.json --svg flame.svg --out annotated-flame.svg`.
   - Acceptance criteria: no sustained Tjunction > 85 C and P99 within 10% of baseline.

2) Controlled in-situ sampling (production shadow)
   - Use sampling window: 10 minute shadow runs covering 1% of traffic from a representative route.
   - Commands: `shadow-run orchestrator --route <route> --sample 0.01 --duration 10m --label thermal-probe-<date>`
   - Collect enriched traces via telemetry-collector and annotate with request provenance (trace id, model-version, kernel-hint).

3) Continuous low-cost probes
   - Probe config (telemetry-collector): sample-rate 0.001 for power/temp + priority-index annotation.
   - Drive alerts on rolling windows (5m/30m) for warning/critical thresholds.

Remediation runbook (elevated Tjunction or power capping detected)

Immediate steps (0–5 minutes):
1. Verify telemetry: `telemetry-cli query --since 5m --filter "node:<node> AND metric:gpu.temp>78" --out quickcheck.json`.
2. If confirmed, mark node as no-new-allocs: `gpu-dispatcher drain --node <node> --mode soft`.
3. Reduce concurrency for affected route(s) via runtime route-policy: set concurrency-limit = 0.5x for the route.
4. Notify on-call SRE team: channel #sre-runtime (post summary, node id, trace references).

Escalation (5–30 minutes):
1. If thermal persists after draining and cooling (5–10 min), trigger controlled model-fallback to lower-power variant (if available): `runtime-kernel-manager fallback --model <model-id> --variant quant-8bit --route <route> --canary 100% --reason "thermal_probe"`.
2. If no fallback and critical thresholds are crossed, escalate to infra to verify rack cooling; file ticket with `infra-ticket create --node <node> --symptoms thermal-critical` and CC runtime SRE.
3. For Dedicated customers, start the SLA incident flow and notify CS as per escalation-playbook.

Post-incident forensics (30–120 minutes)

- Rehydrate traces from telemetry-collector and link to perf-sched traces.
- Run kernel attribution to identify which kernel changes (recent kernel-hint rollouts, new preemption policies, or updated kernels) correlate with increased power draw.
- Produce an incident summary including: timeline, node-id, model-version, kernel-hint configuration, and remediation actions; publish to related_pages above and tag with label `thermal-incident`.

Integration with scheduler / kernel hinting

- Scheduler contract: scheduler may accept `power_budget_hint` and `therm_priority` attributes in the per-request routing header. These are surfaced in runtime-kernel-manager and should be used conservatively. Example header:

```
X-Runtime-Hints: power_budget_hint=120W;therm_priority=low
```

- Guidance:
  - Prefer `power_budget_hint` for long-form streaming requests where a slightly lower power draw trades off repeatable latency vs throughput.
  - Use `therm_priority=high` only during active degradation windows and with operator approval.

Benchmarking protocol additions

- Add a thermal dimension to our standard microbench: include a 45-minute sustained window with controlled ambient temps (if possible) and report: Tjunction time-series, P95/P99 latency vs time, and kernel preemption rates.
- Add a power-capping simulation test that artificially caps GPU power to 80% of TDP and measures latency and failure modes.

Operational tooling and saved queries

- telemetry-collector saved queries:
  - `thermal.warning.recent` => `metric:gpu.temp > 78` rolling 10m
  - `power.capping.detect` => `metric:gpu.power / tdp > 0.95` rolling 5m
- Grafana dashboards: `Runtime / Thermal` dashboard (owner: eng-serving-runtime/dashboard-dot) includes heatmap by rack, node trace links, and per-route thermal exposure.

Ownership and run cadence

- Primary owner: runtime-performance team (rotation: @oncall-runtime-perf).
- Secondary: infra-fleet for rack cooling liaison.
- Quarterly tasks:
  1. Run perf-lab thermal validation for any major kernel or quantization rollout.
  2. Revalidate thresholds after driver updates.

Release gating checklist (kernel or scheduling change impacting power draw)

- Checklist before canary deploy:
  1. Lab synthetic profile executed and passed acceptance criteria.
  2. 10m shadow probe executed against canary and no thermal warning.
  3. Telemetry saved queries configured and verified.
  4. Rollback plan documented and tested (automation for fallback to previously active kernel/hint enabled).

Appendix A: useful commands and snippets

- Quick telemetry query:
```
telemetry-cli query --node node-123 --metrics gpu.temp,gpu.power --since 15m
```
- Mark node soft-drain:
```
gpu-dispatcher drain --node node-123 --mode soft --reason "thermal_probe"
```
- Annotate trace with kernel-hint:
```
span.annotate("kernel_hint", "power_budget:120W")
```

Appendix B: Example incident summary template

1) Title: Thermal degradation — node-123 — 2026-02-27
2) Impacted routes: /v1/generate-chat, /v1/embed
3) Metrics at peak: P99 = 498ms, Tjunction = 91 C, gpu.power = 105% TDP (reported)
4) Actions taken: drained node, reduced route concurrency, triggered quant-8bit fallback for /v1/embed, infra engaged.
5) Root cause: regression in kernel preemption policy causing longer sustained active SM utilization spikes.
6) Follow up: revert policy 1.8.1 -> 1.8.0 on affected canaries; schedule perf-lab replay and driver review.
